text.p: CPC International Inc said on Thursday it expected to have a strong year in 1997, with corn-refining profits returning to normal levels.

"We continue to expect substantial improvements in corn refining profitability in 1997," Chairman C.R. Shoemate said. He said the company had liquidated essentially all of its corn futures positions in 1997.
CPC said the cost of liquidating the corn futures positions was absorbed in 1996 and offset by lower current taxes than previously forecast and a reversal of tax reserves.
It said it expected to earn $3.93 per share in 1996, and to benefit from a tax rate lower than 37 percent in 1997.
CPC said corn refining accounted for less than 15 percent of the company's total earnings.
Consumer foods and baking, its largest business segments, had a good year, Shoemate said.

"We have had an outstanding year in consumer foods and baking, and more strategic action is underway around the world now than ever before to build these businesses aggressively," he said. "The results are clearly evident in 1996 and will be again in 1997."
